answers.visit_reason: I am here for a follow-up appointment about my high blood pressure and diabetes. I have been feeling more tired than usual, especially in the afternoons. I am also concerned that my blood sugar might be getting worse.
answers.top_concern: I am worried about developing complications from diabetes because my mother had diabetes and eventually developed kidney problems.
answers.patient_questions: Do I need to change my medications? What can I do to improve my blood sugar without completely changing my diet? How often should I check my blood pressure?
answers.family_history: Mother: Type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease. Father: Hypertension and heart attack at age 68
answers.medications:
Medication	Dose	Frequency
Metformin	1,000 mg	Twice daily
Lisinopril	10 mg	Once daily
Atorvastatin	20 mg	Once daily
answers.other_clinicians: Ophthalmologist for annual diabetic eye exams
answers.symptoms_details: I have been feeling tired around 2 or 3 PM almost every day. I sometimes wake up at night to use the bathroom. I have also been getting mild headaches a few times per week.
answers.activity: I walk about 15 minutes during my lunch break three days per week. I do not have a regular exercise routine outside of work.
answers.food: I usually eat cereal or toast for breakfast. I bring a sandwich or leftovers for lunch. Dinner is often rice, chicken, and vegetables. I enjoy traditional family meals and would prefer not to give up foods I grew up eating.
answers.work_schedule: I work Monday through Friday from 7:30 AM to 4 PM. I have limited time for appointments during the school year.
answers.support: I live with my husband and teenage daughter. My husband usually prepares dinner, and we often eat together as a family.
answers.barriers_details: My biggest challenges are finding time to exercise, remembering to take medications during busy mornings, and preparing healthy meals that my entire family will enjoy.
answers.preferred_changes: I would be willing to walk for 20 minutes after dinner with my husband, reduce sugary drinks, and make small changes to our family meals. I would prefer gradual changes instead of a strict diet.
answers.learning_style: Simple explanations with a little detail
answers.goal: I prefer simple language with specific instructions. I would like to understand why I am taking each medication and what I should do if something goes wrong.
